notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-24/25, about 120 queries total. Quiet day: no genuine new same-day (Oct 24/25) announcement surfaced in any lane that wasn't SEO filler or already filed. Most forward-looking candidates each lane surfaced turned out, on cross-check against the full corpus, to already be on file at matching or better date/confidence/completeness; several devtools/cloud candidates (JDK 28 GA, Kubernetes 1.36 EOL, Google Cloud Next 2027 including endDate+location, KubeCon Europe 2027 including endDate+location, GitHub Enterprise Server 3.20, Docker Hub Automated Builds, AWS Lambda Node.js 22 deprecation) were verified field-by-field against the existing entries and found to add nothing a refile would improve, so none were re-filed. The AI lane found three new Anthropic model-support-floor dates (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8) on Anthropic's own model-deprecations page, sitting alongside the already-filed Opus 4.6 entry but not yet captured. A dry run of apply-findings showed all three would incorrectly collapse into the existing Opus 4.6 entry (see concerns), so they were dropped from this run rather than risk destroying data. What this run actually filed: one new CISA KEV remediation deadline (CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell flaw patched in the October 2026 Patch Tuesday and exploited to bypass Mark of the Web) that prior runs had queried for but never filed.
concerns: Found a concrete, reproducible instance of the sameTitle/sameOrg dedupe gap in src/lib/id.ts that goes beyond cosmetic duplicates: it actively destroys data. isSameThing() treats 'Claude Opus 4.6 reaches minimum guaranteed support floor' (2027-02-05, already on file) as the same real-world thing as 'Claude Sonnet 4.6 reaches minimum guaranteed support floor' (2027-02-17), 'Claude Opus 4.7 reaches minimum guaranteed support floor' (2027-04-16), and 'Claude Opus 4.8 reaches minimum guaranteed support floor' (2027-05-28), because sameTitle's 0.6 token-overlap threshold doesn't weight the model-name/version tokens (opus/sonnet, 4/6/7/8) heavily enough against the five shared boilerplate words (reaches minimum guaranteed support floor), and EVENT_DRIFT_DAYS=75 lets each successive merge's updated date creep far enough to catch the next one in a chain (Feb 5 to Feb 17 to Apr 16 to May 28, each step under 75 days from the last). Verified with: npx tsx scripts/apply-findings.ts findings.json --dry-run, filing all three as separate findings and confirming all three merge into the single existing Opus 4.6 entry, overwriting its date and title each time rather than creating three new rows. Dropped them from this run's entries; their facts are recorded here so a maintainer can file them once isSameThing is fixed to also require version-token agreement for titles that are otherwise near-identical boilerplate: Claude Sonnet 4.6 support floor 2027-02-17, Claude Opus 4.7 support floor 2027-04-16, Claude Opus 4.8 support floor 2027-05-28, all sourced from https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations.
